Uma Versus Wiki

Update 1.8 · build a61915

Welcome to the Uma Versus wiki, the reference for the fan-made Umamusume browser fighting game: characters, moves, frame data and combos. All frame data and combos are measured from the game itself, so they match build a61915.

Characters

Archetypes

ArchetypePlays likeCharacters
All-RounderA little of everything. Has a tool for every range: a projectile, an anti-air, a way in and a way to defend. Rarely loses a matchup outright, but also rarely wins one on paper. Good for learning the game and for adapting mid-match.Special Week
Hit and RunGet in, hit, get out. Darts in for one clean hit, then leaves before the opponent can answer. High damage and strong escape tools, balanced by low health and few ways to defend once cornered.Silence Suzuka
RushdownStay in their face. Fast, plus-on-block attacks and ways to keep a turn going after it is blocked. Wants to start pressure and never let it end; struggles when forced to play from a distance.Gold Ship
VortexKnock down, then make them guess. Built around knockdowns that remove the defender's wake-up options, followed by a 50/50: in front or behind, high or low, strike or throw. A wrong guess leads back to another knockdown.Vodka
Bait and PunishMake them commit, then make them pay. Waits for the opponent to act first. Long pokes, a counter stance and extra damage on recovering opponents turn every mistake into a big punish. Has few ways to start offense alone, and once the opponent stops taking the bait it has to work hard.Mejiro McQueen
Glass CannonWin fast or lose fast. Turns a single opening into huge damage, but has the least health and almost no defensive tools. Every exchange matters: the round can be over in two combos either way.Tokai Teio
ShotoThe classic toolkit. A projectile, an invincible uppercut and an advancing attack, in the tradition of Street Fighter's Ryu and Ken. Easy to pick up and solid in every matchup, but the game plan is predictable.Kitasan Black
ZonerControl the screen. Keeps the opponent at a distance with projectiles at different angles and speeds. Low damage, so wins come from many small hits and from denying the opponent a way in.Daiwa Scarlet

Reference

How to play

Default controls

Every input can be rebound from Controls in the main menu (saved in your browser).

ActionPlayer 1Player 2Gamepad
Move / jump / crouchW A S DArrow keysD-pad / left stick
Light (L)FJ or Num1X / □
Medium (M)GK or Num2Y / △
Heavy (H)HL or Num3B / ○
Skill (S)TI or Num5A / ✕
Throw (L+M)RU or Num4LB
Super (S+H)YO or Num6RB
Taunt (L+H)EP or Num7Back
PauseEsc / Start

Notation

Directions use the numpad, as if the character faces right: 5 neutral, 2 down, 6 forward, 4 back. 5M is a standing medium, 2M a crouching medium, j.H a jumping heavy. 236 is ↓↘→, 623 is →↓↘, 214 is ↓↙←, 41236 is ←↙↓↘→. In combos, › means cancel or link into the next move.

Defense

  • Block by holding back. Hold down-back to block lows. Overheads (jumping attacks, hop moves, dive kicks) must be blocked standing.
  • You can block straight out of a dash: holding back cancels the dash immediately.
  • Throw with L+M up close; hold back for a back throw. Throws beat blocking. Escape a throw by pressing L+M as it connects (command grabs cannot be escaped).
  • Counter Spurt: press S+H while blocking to spend 50 Spurt on an invincible push-away.
  • Backdash (←←) is briefly invincible.
  • Wake-up: hold any attack button while knocked down to get up early, or hold ↓ to get up late. Hard knockdowns (throws, command grabs, supers, and some skills such as Vodka's Full Throttle) disable both.

Skills and the Spurt gauge

  • Do a skill's motion with L or M for its two free versions. With H it becomes the EX version, which costs 50 Spurt. Without 50 Spurt, H gives the M version.
  • The S + direction shortcut (S, →S, ←S, ↓S) does the M version without a motion, at the cost of a cooldown and 10% less damage.
  • The Spurt gauge fills as you deal and take damage. It pays for EX skills (50), Counter Spurt (50), Gold Ship's dash cancel (10) and supers (100, S+H).

Combos

  • Chains: normals cancel into stronger normals: L › M › H.
  • Auto-combo: on hit, mash L for 5L › 5M › 5H › skill.
  • Skill cancels: any normal that connects can be cancelled into a skill or super.
  • Jump cancel: after a launching hit (2H, or the second hit of 5H), hold ↑ to jump after them for an air combo.
  • The input buffer is 9 frames. A buffered button remembers the direction and motion you entered when you pressed it, so inputs made during hit freeze still come out as intended.

Combo scaling and limits

  • Damage scaling: the first hit of a combo does full damage. After that, damage depends on what started the combo (a light starter: 80%, a medium: 90%, a heavy, counter hit or punish: 100%), and drops by a further 13% per hit from the 3rd hit, down to 25%. Supers always keep at least 50%. The combo counter shows the scaling for the next hit.
  • Juggle points: every hit on an airborne opponent costs juggle points (normals 1, skills 2, bounces 1). At 10 the opponent can no longer be hit in the air.
  • Ground bounce: j.H in an air combo slams the opponent into the ground and they bounce back up, so you can relaunch them (2H) after you land. Once per combo.
  • Wall bounce: several EX knockdowns bounce the opponent off the corner or the edge of the screen, ready for a follow-up. Once per combo.
  • Hitstun decay: after a combo has lasted 2 seconds, each new hit causes less hitstun and juggled opponents fall faster, so loops eventually drop.
  • Combo limit: after 32 hits or 7 seconds, further hits pass through and the opponent drops out. This makes infinites impossible.
  • In combo notation, link means wait until you recover, then start the next move (it can't be cancelled into).

Movement

  • Double-tap → to dash and ←← to backdash. Press L, M or H during a dash, or input →→ + button, for a dash attack: L jab, M lunge, H leaping overhead kick.
  • →+M is a hop overhead. Low attacks beat it because you are briefly airborne.
  • Only Silence Suzuka can air dash. It needs some height, cannot attack for the first 8 frames, and has landing recovery.

Accounts

  • Accounts are optional: guests can play every mode. Make one from Account on the main menu with an email, a password, a display name (3–16 letters, numbers, spaces, _ . -) and a favourite runner.
  • Online name: your display name is shown to your opponent in the lobby and during the match.
  • Cloud save: controls, volume, Options and combo-trial progress are saved to your account every few seconds and come back when you sign in on another browser or computer.
  • Match history: every online match you finish while signed in is saved, with your record, win rate and most-played runner on the Account screen. VS CPU matches are not counted, so they can't pad anyone's win rate.
  • Change your name or favourite runner, save now, or sign out from the Account screen.

Training, replays and online

  • Training shows damage, combo scaling, juggle points, frame advantage and hitboxes. Keys: 1 dummy · 2 dummy guard · 3 hitboxes · 4 reset · 5 input display · 6 frame meter · 7 record the dummy · 8 play the recording back.
  • Frame meter: one cell per frame for both players, coloured by startup (green), active (red), recovery (blue), hit or block stun (yellow) and outlined when invincible, plus the startup of your move and the frame advantage.
  • Dummy record & playback: press 7 to control the dummy and record up to 10 seconds, 7 again to stop, then 8 to have the dummy loop it while you practice blocking or punishing.
  • Combo trials: every runner's combos as challenges the game checks for you, with a demo (9) that performs each one. Cleared trials are saved in your browser.
  • Replays: every Versus, VS CPU and Online match is recorded. Press R on the results screen to watch, or D to save a file.
  • Online uses rollback netcode and room codes. Both players need the same build: this wiki matches build a61915.

Special Week is the all-rounder of the cast. A fireball, an uppercut, an advancing spin and an armored tackle. A bit of everything.

Contents

  1. Overview
  2. Normal moves
  3. Skills
  4. Super
  5. Combos

Overview

All-Rounder: A little of everything. Has a tool for every range: a projectile, an anti-air, a way in and a way to defend. Rarely loses a matchup outright, but also rarely wins one on paper. Good for learning the game and for adapting mid-match.

Special Week has an answer at every range. Dream Shot controls the middle of the screen, Rising Dream stops jump-ins, Spurt Tornado travels in and passes over low pokes, and Last Spurt Tackle armors through a single hit or projectile to close distance.

The game plan is to play to whatever the opponent is weak against. Against a zoner, walk behind L Dream Shot and armor through their shots with Tackle. Against rushdown, block, then reversal with Rising Dream.

Strengths

  • Tools for every situation
  • Fully invincible EX Rising Dream
  • Straightforward combos that end in a knockdown

Weaknesses

  • Specialists beat her at their own game
  • Rising Dream and Last Spurt Tackle are very punishable if blocked

Silence Suzuka is the hit and run of the cast. Get in, hit hard, get out. Big damage, great escapes, low health.

Contents

  1. Overview
  2. Normal moves
  3. Skills
  4. Super
  5. Combos
  6. Tips

Overview

Hit and Run: Get in, hit, get out. Darts in for one clean hit, then leaves before the opponent can answer. High damage and strong escape tools, balanced by low health and few ways to defend once cornered.

Land one clean hit, then leave. Great Escape (M) runs through the opponent and keeps going, and Silent Flicker kicks then hops far back, so many of her moves are minus on paper but safe because she ends up out of reach.

Her damage per hit (×1.1) is second only to Tokai Teio, and she moves fast: a quick dash, a long invincible backdash and an air dash. The cost is 8,500 health and a weak reversal, so getting cornered is dangerous.

Strengths

  • High damage per hit (×1.1, second only to Teio)
  • Moves that leave her out of punish range
  • Air dash and a long invincible backdash

Weaknesses

  • Second-lowest health in the cast (8,500)
  • Lead the Pack has little invincibility, especially the L version
  • Few options once she is pinned in a corner

Tips

  • Great Escape L stops in front, M runs through. Mixing the two makes them hard to punish on reaction.

  5. Combos
  6. Tips

Overview

Rushdown: Stay in their face. Fast, plus-on-block attacks and ways to keep a turn going after it is blocked. Wants to start pressure and never let it end; struggles when forced to play from a distance.

Gold Ship wants to start her turn and keep it. Her 5L comes out in 4 frames, recovers faster than anyone else's and is plus on block (+2), crouching jabs chain into themselves, and Barrage is plus on block too.

Golshi Rush is the mixup engine: during the dash, choose a low slide, an overhead hop chop, an untechable command grab, or stop dead and do something else. Dash cancels (→→ after a normal, 10 Spurt) keep pressure going after a blocked string.

Strengths

  • Fastest normals in the game (4f 5L, 6f 5M)
  • Plus-on-block pressure tools
  • Four-way command dash mixup

Weaknesses

  • No invincible reversal attack (only EX Golshi Rush is invincible, and it is a dash)
  • Golshi Dropkick!! is about −22 on block
  • Struggles against keep-away at long range

Vodka is the vortex of the cast. Score a hard knockdown, then make them guess: in front, behind, high, low or grab.

Contents

  1. Overview
  2. Normal moves
  3. Skills
  4. Super
  5. Combos
  6. Tips

Overview

Vortex: Knock down, then make them guess. Built around knockdowns that remove the defender's wake-up options, followed by a 50/50: in front or behind, high or low, strike or throw. A wrong guess leads back to another knockdown.

Vodka's loop starts with a hard knockdown: Full Throttle, the Pit Stop command grab, or the EX versions of Drift Hop and Drift Drop. A hard knockdown cannot be quick-risen, so the opponent always gets up at the same time and her setups line up.

On their wake-up, make them guess. Drift Hop L lands in front and M crosses over. A meaty 2L is low, Drift Drop and j.M are overheads, and a walk-up Pit Stop beats blocking. A wrong guess leads into another hard knockdown.

Strengths

  • Consistent wake-up setups after hard knockdowns
  • Cross-up jumping attacks (j.L / j.M hit behind her)
  • Untechable command grab

Weaknesses

  • Rev Kick only beats air attacks, it is not invincible on the ground
  • Average neutral game: she has to earn the first knockdown
  • Patterns become readable if you never vary them

Daiwa Scarlet is the zoner of the cast. Shots straight, up, low and from the air, plus a barrier that reflects. Low damage up close.

Contents

  1. Overview
  2. Normal moves
  3. Skills
  4. Super
  5. Combos
  6. Tips

Overview

Zoner: Control the screen. Keeps the opponent at a distance with projectiles at different angles and speeds. Low damage, so wins come from many small hits and from denying the opponent a way in.

Daiwa keeps the opponent where she wants them. Scarlet Shot goes straight (two can be on screen), High Top Line angles upward to stop jumps, Ground Rose travels low along the ground, and Sky Shot fires downward from a jump.

Rose Barrier reflects incoming projectiles and knocks away anyone too close, which sends them back to shooting range. Her damage is the lowest in the cast (×0.88) and her dash is slow, so she wins through many small hits.

Strengths

  • Projectiles at four different angles
  • Reflector that also pushes people away
  • Long-reaching normals and a strong backdash

Weaknesses

  • Lowest damage (×0.88)
  • Slowest dash
  • Struggles once an opponent is up close

Uma Versus › Characters › Mejiro McQueen

Mejiro McQueen

From Uma Versus Wiki · build a61915

Mejiro McQueen
ArchetypeBait and Punish

Mejiro McQueen is the bait and punish of the cast. Long pokes, a counter stance, and extra damage on anyone caught recovering.

Contents

  1. Overview
  2. Normal moves
  3. Skills
  4. Super
  5. Combos
  6. Tips

Overview

Bait and Punish: Make them commit, then make them pay. Waits for the opponent to act first. Long pokes, a counter stance and extra damage on recovering opponents turn every mistake into a big punish. Has few ways to start offense alone, and once the opponent stops taking the bait it has to work hard.

McQueen wants the opponent to move first. Her 5M and Stayer's Lance reach further than almost anything in the game, so walking toward her is risky, and anyone who throws out an attack up close may run into Noble Parry.

Her passive, Punish, adds 20% damage and extra hitstun to the first hit on an opponent who is recovering from a move or a long landing. Whiffed specials, blocked unsafe moves and badly spaced jump-ins all turn into big damage. Long-Distance Stride covers the far end of the screen, and its EX passes through projectiles.

Strengths

  • Very long pokes: Stayer's Lance has the longest reach of any poke
  • Counter stance that catches any strike, high or low
  • Highest health (10,500) and PUNISH! damage

Weaknesses

  • Little offense of her own
  • Noble Parry loses to throws and (except EX) projectiles
  • A patient opponent who stops attacking takes away her game

Tokai Teio is the glass cannon of the cast. Her specials chain into each other for huge damage, but she has the lowest health.

Contents

  1. Overview
  2. Normal moves
  3. Skills
  4. Super
  5. Combos
  6. Tips

Overview

Glass Cannon: Win fast or lose fast. Turns a single opening into huge damage, but has the least health and almost no defensive tools. Every exchange matters: the round can be over in two combos either way.

Teio turns one hit into a lot of damage. Her specials can chain into each other on hit: after the last hit of one skill, input another and it comes out immediately. Each skill can be used once per combo, so a full chain looks like Teio Step › Imperial Rush › Emperor's Rise.

Her health is the lowest in the game (8,000) and Emperor's Rise is not invincible unless you spend meter, so her defense is thin. When her health drops below 30%, Miracle Mode adds 15% damage for a last-ditch comeback.

Strengths

  • Highest damage in the cast (×1.12) and the biggest combos
  • Specials chain into each other on hit
  • Miracle Mode comeback below 30% health

Weaknesses

  • Lowest health (8,000)
  • No invincible reversal without meter
  • Chains only work on hit: a blocked special is just a blocked special

Kitasan Black is the shoto of the cast. The textbook kit: a fireball, an invincible uppercut, a spinning kick (also in the air) and a step-in punch.

Contents

  1. Overview
  2. Normal moves
  3. Skills
  4. Super
  5. Combos
  6. Tips

Overview

Shoto: The classic toolkit. A projectile, an invincible uppercut and an advancing attack, in the tradition of Street Fighter's Ryu and Ken. Easy to pick up and solid in every matchup, but the game plan is predictable.

Kitasan is the textbook shoto. Festival Drum is a fireball with quick recovery, Matsuri Uppercut is the strongest invincible reversal in the cast, Festival Whirlwind travels in and passes over lows, and Kitasan Straight is a nearly safe step-in punch.

The plan is the classic one: throw fireballs to make the opponent jump, uppercut the jump, and use the step-in and whirlwind to take your turn up close. Special Week shares some tools but plays as an all-rounder; Kitasan has the stronger fundamentals and the more predictable game plan.

Strengths

  • Fast-recovering fireball (28 frames total)
  • Strongest invincible uppercut (1,300 damage)
  • Whirlwind works on the ground and in the air

Weaknesses

  • Predictable once the opponent learns the pattern
  • Matsuri Uppercut is very punishable if blocked
  • No armor or counter tools

  • Costs the full Spurt gauge (100).

Combos

These are the runner's combo trials (★ = advanced). Every one is performed by the game's own demo and test suite on build a61915. Damage is against a full-health opponent with the current scaling.

Tips

  • L Festival Drum is slow enough to walk behind.
  • Sky Whirlwind is an overhead that changes your jump arc.
  • Kitasan Straight is only slightly minus on block. End blocked strings with it to keep pressure.

Stages

From Uma Versus Wiki · build a61915

Pick a course after both runners are entered, or leave it to the draw with Random. Stages are cosmetic: every course has the same size and floor, so matchups play the same everywhere. Online, the host picks the course from the entry screen (↑ / ↓).

Update 1.8

Patch notes · build a61915

Accounts

  • New Account entry on the main menu. Accounts are optional: guests can still play everything.
  • Sign up with an email, a password, a display name and a favourite runner. Names are unique, 3–16 characters long.
  • Your name online: opponents see your display name in the lobby and during the match.
  • Cloud save: controls, volume, Options and combo-trial progress follow you to any browser. The first time you sign in, the settings in that browser become your account's.
  • Match history: online matches are saved while you're signed in. The Account screen shows your online record (matches, wins, losses, win rate), most-played runner and your last few results. VS CPU matches are never recorded, so they can't inflate a win rate.
  • The title screen shows who is signed in.

Sharper picture

  • The game now draws at your screen's real resolution instead of stretching a 960×540 image, so text, menus, the HUD and the logo are sharp at any window size and on high-DPI screens. Sprites keep their pixel-art look.
  • New option Sharp text (high resolution) in Options. Turn it off on a slow computer to go back to the classic low-resolution picture.

Privacy

  • Your email and password are only used to sign in and are never shown to anyone. Your display name, favourite runner and match results are public, so other players can see them. Settings are private to your account.
  • Each player can only add results to their own history.

Online

  • Both players need build a61915.

Update 1.7

Patch notes · build a61915

New logo

  • Uma Versus has a logo: the U of UMA is a horseshoe, with the starting-gate colours as speed stripes. It's on the title screen, the top bar of every menu, and this wiki.
  • The game also has its own icon in the browser tab: the horseshoe U.

Daiwa Scarlet

  • Number One Finish is now her own super instead of a rush. Daiwa fires a volley of five golden roses followed by a big finishing rose. Each shot is a separate projectile that can hit, be blocked or miss on its own. Fully connected it does about 2,300 damage, close to the cast average, and ends in a hard knockdown; from full screen, or against a juggled or crouching opponent, some shots can fly past.
  • Super shots go through normal projectiles, can't be reflected and don't use juggle points. Up close it's punishable on block; from range it's safe. See Daiwa Scarlet.
  • The CPU uses it as a punish from range and against opponents who dash or jump in from far away.

Fixes

  • Gold Ship could fly off the top of the screen if Golshi Dropkick!! was cancelled into a super while she was in the air. Suzuka's Silent Flicker had the same problem. A grounded move now always falls back to the floor.
  • If a super's cinematic was cut short (for example by time running out), the opponent could stay frozen and the match never finished. The super's user is now invincible during the cinematic, and the opponent is always released.
  • A super cinematic near the edge of the stage could push the opponent outside the stage.
  • A projectile already in the air could hit a runner in the middle of a throw, leaving the thrown opponent frozen and the match stuck. Throws in progress are now protected, like super cinematics.
  • Resetting Training (4) during a super flash could crash the game or leave it frozen.
  • The cinematic part of every super ignored the runner's damage multiplier and Teio's Miracle Mode. Supers now use the same multipliers as every other hit, so Suzuka (×1.1) and Teio (×1.12) supers hit a little harder.
  • The wiki's super damage is now measured in the game for a fresh hit, with scaling, instead of adding up the raw numbers.

Testing

  • New stress tests run thousands of random matches across all 64 matchups and press random keys through every menu, checking that nothing crashes, freezes or leaves the stage.

Online

  • Both players need build a61915.

Update 1.6

Patch notes · build a61915

New look

  • Every menu and the in-game HUD were redesigned around race day: starting-gate colours for each runner, tote-board LED timers and results, saddlecloth name plates and rosettes for round wins.
  • New screens: course select, a race-card VS splash before each match, and an official result board after it.
  • Rounds now start with the starting gate opening on GO!, and knockouts end in a photo finish.

Stages

  • Three new courses: Tracen Training Track (sunset), Nakayama Nights (winter night race with snow) and Winning Live (concert stage), alongside Tokyo Racecourse. See Stages.
  • Replays remember their stage. Online, the host picks the course.

Music

  • Music for the whole game: a Menu Theme, a theme for each of the eight runners, and a Third Round Theme.
  • After the course select, P1 picks the battle theme. It defaults to P1's runner and can be swapped to any character theme (the selector previews each one). Online, the host (P1) picks it in the lobby.
  • The character theme fades in as round 1 starts and keeps playing into round 2. If the match goes to a tie-breaking final round, it fades out during the round 2 KO and the Third Round Theme fades in with the countdown. Music fades out at the end of the match.
  • Music and effects volume (saved in your browser) and every track to listen to are in Options on the main menu. Music volume is also in the pause menu.
  • Replays remember which theme was playing.

Combos

  • New damage scaling based on the starter (light 80%, medium 90%, heavy, counter hit or punish 100%) with a 13% drop per hit from the 3rd hit, down to 25%. Supers keep at least 50%.
  • Ground bounce (j.H in an air combo) and wall bounce (several EX knockdowns), once each per combo, for longer routes.
  • Juggle points instead of a hit count, hitstun decay after 2 seconds, and a hard combo limit of 32 hits or 7 seconds, so infinites are impossible.
  • The combo counter shows the scaling of the next hit. See How to play.

Training

  • Combo Trials mode: 51 trials across the cast, including advanced routes with bounces, each with a demo the game performs for you.
  • Input display, frame meter, and dummy record & playback in Training.
  • The Training readout shows combo scaling and juggle points.

Quality of life

  • Rematch from the results screen (same runners, course and music), or go to character select or the main menu.
  • Random runner slot on every character select, including online. Cursors start on the runners you picked last time.
  • Options: music and effects volume, Reduce flashes & shake, fullscreen, and every track. Reduce flashes and fullscreen are in the pause menu too.
  • The online room panel can be used with a gamepad: ↑ ↓ to move, A to press, and in the code box ↑ ↓ change the letter and ← → move along.
  • Menu sounds: move, confirm, back, the ENTERED stamp, a race bell and the starting gate at the start of each round, and a fanfare for results and cleared trials.

CPU

  • The CPU was rebuilt. It now has four levels, ROOKIE, NORMAL, HARD and G1, picked with ← → on VS CPU in the main menu.
  • It reacts to what it sees with a human-like delay (from about 24 frames on Rookie to 8 on G1) instead of reading inputs, and blocks high or low by guessing, so mix-ups work on it.
  • Higher levels hit-confirm the same routes as the Combo Trials, punish unsafe moves, anti-air jump-ins, tech throws and jump or dash past projectiles.
  • Each runner plays to their archetype: zoners keep away with projectiles, Suzuka hits and runs, bait characters wait for a whiff, and vortex characters press their knockdowns.

Fixes

  • The CPU could use its super while airborne or right out of hitstun. Its reversals and supers now have a human delay after it recovers, and it only goes for a super when it can reach a grounded opponent.
  • Supers at the end of a combo are reliable: if the first hit lands, the full cinematic plays, including on a juggled opponent (for example Teio's 5L 5M 5H 5L › super).
  • The Menu Theme starts on the first key press, click or tap (browsers block sound before that). If the browser is still holding it back, the title screen says so.
  • Leaving a match during a KO could make the next match skip counting a round win.
  • Some of Tokai Teio's frames showed a green square behind her.

Online

  • Both players need build a61915.

Patch notes · build a61915

Update 1.5

Team Spica is complete: three new characters bring the roster to eight.

New characters

  • Mejiro McQueen (Bait and Punish): long pokes, the Noble Parry counter stance, and the Punish passive (+20% damage on recovering opponents). Highest health in the cast.
  • Tokai Teio (Glass Cannon): specials chain into each other on hit for the biggest combos in the game. Lowest health, no free reversal, and Miracle Mode below 30% health.
  • Kitasan Black (Shoto): fireball, invincible uppercut, a whirlwind kick on the ground and in the air, and a step-in punch.

Systems

  • New move properties: counter stances, passing through projectiles (several EX moves), special chains and comeback damage.
  • Move list shows each character's passive traits.
  • CPU: McQueen's CPU waits, pokes and uses Noble Parry when you swing up close.

Online

  • Both players need build a61915. Older builds are refused at connect.

Patch notes · build a61915

Update 1

New

  • Three new characters: Gold Ship (Rushdown), Vodka (Vortex) and Daiwa Scarlet (Zoner).
  • Control mapping for both keyboard layouts and gamepads, saved in your browser.
  • Unique animation profiles for every character: timing, taunts, intros, win poses and signature effects.
  • A Combos page in the in-game move list, and this wiki.

Gameplay

  • EX rework: motion + L and M are the free versions; motion + H is the EX and costs 50 Spurt. The Skill button no longer triggers EX.
  • Guard button removed: block by holding back. Taunt moved to L+H.
  • Blocking out of a dash: holding back cancels a dash instantly.
  • Movement: walk and dash speeds brought closer together, backdash invincibility shortened (4 frames for most), double jump removed, and air dash now needs height, cannot attack for 8 frames and has landing recovery.
  • Combos: 9-frame input buffer that remembers your direction and motion, slightly more hitstun on normals, less pushback on hit, more lenient juggles, higher 5H launchers, and jump cancels only after a launching hit.
  • Projectiles can now travel at angles, along the ground, from the air, two at a time, and be reflected.

Characters

  • Special Week is now an All-Rounder: Guts! is replaced by Last Spurt Tackle, an armored charge.
  • Silence Suzuka is now Hit and Run: new Silent Flicker (kick, then hop away), Turbine Roll moved to ←↙↓↘→, teleport and double jump removed, damage +10%, health 8,500.
  • Gold Ship: H versions of her skills are now EX versions.
